item.title: 2026.11.09-beta
item.description:
## What's new
- FazerWM now has its own per-window fullscreen. Press ctrl+cmd+f or click the green button and the window goes fullscreen under FazerWM's layout, with a badge on the tab indicator, Overview, and Recent Windows. - Slow macOS animations suck! Now they're instant - Native fullscreen is taken over: the system fullscreen gesture, the Enter/Exit Full Screen menu item, and windows already in native fullscreen convert to FazerWM fullscreen instead. - Native minimized is taken over: the yellow button or cmd+M, and a floating window can be zoomed into the tiling. Minimized and fullscreen windows are restored to their state on relaunch.
## Fixes
- Fixed the app going unresponsive for 10 to 20 seconds, leaving hotkeys and the menu bar dead, while it scanned other applications' windows. - Launch is much faster, and clicking windows no longer stalls for seconds. - After a reboot, session restore now matches relaunched windows whose titles changed, so a second Mail window lands in its saved spot instead of where macOS reopened it. - Recent Windows cards are sized from the window again instead of the display, which happened when another window of the same app was fullscreen. - Windows of the frontmost app now park correctly; a fullscreen seat beside a focused compose window used to sit unparked underneath it.
Also includes internal improvements.

## What's new
- Session restore (Pro). FazerWM saves your layout as you work and puts it back after a FazerWM restart, a reboot or a logout: each window returns to its display, workspace and column, stacked and tabbed columns regroup, manual widths and floating positions come back, and the window you were using gets focus again. After a reboot it waits up to a minute for your apps to reopen their windows and shows a "Restoring your layout" panel while it places them. Plugging in a display setup you have used before moves windows back to the displays they were on, and a setup it has not seen is laid out from the most recent one. - macOS native fullscreen now works alongside the tiling layout. A fullscreen window keeps its column, with a placeholder holding the gap on the desktop and in the Overview, and fullscreen windows show an icon in Recent Windows. Leaving fullscreen puts the window back in its column and takes you to its workspace. Starting FazerWM while an app is fullscreen now finds the windows on the desktop behind it. Window rules take precedence over fullscreen: the green button on a rule-managed window shows a short note instead. - Minimizing windows works. A minimized window leaves its column and the others close up. Restoring it from the Dock, Recent Windows or the Overview brings it back as a new column after the focused window, on that window's display, and focuses it. Minimizing the focused window passes focus on the way closing one does. The Overview shows minimized windows along the bottom edge of each display: hover one to see it in full, click to restore. - Overview column drags (Pro). Hold the column-drag modifier while dragging a thumbnail to move a whole column, with stacked windows and tab indicators carried along. The drag keeps going when you close the Overview mid-drag or carry it onto the desktop. Dropping a column on another column's middle merges it as a stack or as tabs. Dragging from desktop to Overview works as well. - The Recent Windows switcher can take over ⌘Tab, ⌘⇧Tab, ⌘` and ⌘⇧` (Pro, off by default). - Overview window labels and app icons in the Recent Windows switcher are new Pro features. - The trial-ended dialog and the Pro tab link to the full Free vs Pro table. - FazerWM launches faster. Windows are tiled about 45 percent sooner, the menu bar icon and login-item setup no longer delay the first layout, and keybinds and gestures stay responsive while it starts.
## Fixes
- Fixed-size windows such as balenaEtcher no longer flick between sizes or make the focus ring jitter, and windows with a minimum height such as Bambu Studio are no longer fought over their size. - Pointer follows focus now lands inside the window when you focus a column that was off screen. - Apps hidden with ⌘H come back when their window returns to the visible layout. Before, the window could stay invisible until you focused it. - A window that an app rebuilds, such as an Electron reload, now returns to its tile instead of staying invisible. - A quick click on a title bar no longer switches workspaces or hides the windows you were looking at. - Dropping a window in the gap between stacked windows now inserts it between them. - Switching workspaces with a keybind while dragging now refreshes the drop zones, so the drop lands on the workspace you can see. - Closing the Overview in the middle of a drag no longer leaves it blank the next time you open it. - Fixed a crash when dragging a window across displays.
Also includes internal improvements.

item.title: 2026.10.29-beta
item.description:
## What's new
- Added an opt-in setting (Pro) that puts the recent windows switcher on ⌘Tab, ⌘⇧Tab, ⌘` and ⌘⇧` in place of the macOS switcher. - Overview thumbnails now carry a label showing the app icon and window title, so windows are easier to tell apart at a glance. (Pro) Configure them under Settings > Overview > Window Labels. - Recent windows cards show the app icon next to the app name. (Pro) Toggle it under Settings > Recent Windows.
## Fixes
- Fixed a wake bug where a display's windows could end up on another display and stay there after the display returned, leaving conflicting layouts and an empty desktop. - Windows keep their display and workspace assignments through brief display reconfigurations, such as waking from sleep or switching inputs. - Dragging a file or selected text out of a window no longer brings up the drop-zone overlay when the pointer crosses onto another display. - Apps that insist on their own window size, like a browser restoring its previous session, are now sized correctly instead of keeping the wrong height. - Reopening the overview no longer shows a stale app label or a stuck expanded label.
Also includes internal improvements.

FazerWM is a keyboard-driven tiling window manager for macOS.
- Windows tile into columns you drive from the keyboard: focus, move, resize, and reorder without touching the mouse. Vi- and Emacs-style keybind presets ship in the box. - Each display has its own workspaces, so different projects stay on different screens. Switch with a keystroke. Can be coupled in settings. - One keypress opens the overview: every workspace on every display at once, as thumbnails you can click to jump to. - Dragging works too. Labeled drop zones offer a new column or a stack, with more options under Pro. - Native macOS tab groups are managed as one window: they tile, move, and park together, and a column can hold tabs of its own. - Rules can send an app to a given workspace or column the moment it opens, matched by app, window title, or pattern. - Trackpad gestures and a recent-windows switcher sit alongside the keybinds. - Multi-display layouts survive a monitor going to sleep or reconnecting one screen at a time; columns and their order stay put. - A first-run wizard explains the two macOS permissions and what each one is for before asking for them. - FazerWM is free to use, tiling up to eight windows in a single workspace, and every install starts with a Pro trial. - Pro adds more workspaces and the fuller set of drag actions: drop as a tab, drag whole columns, pause at a display edge to switch workspaces mid-drag, or continue a drag inside the overview.
